content.text:
Here’s what changed across **several passes** (all in the same repo tree you’re using with Playwright).

### Pass 1 — CI-style flakes (palette, mission control, sweeps)

- **`e2e/ui-controls-sweep.spec.js` — `clickIfVisible`**  
  Normal click → **forced** click → **`dispatchEvent('click')`** in the page, so toolbar hits survive “visible but never receives click” / z-index cases (same class of failure as **`mission-control-open-btn`** in your logs).

- **Primary top-bar sweep**  
  Scroll the status bar into view, **`dismissBlockingOverlays`** before and between buttons, slightly shorter post-`Escape` delay.

- **`e2e/react-core.spec.js` — Command palette**  
  Overlay dismiss, **scroll** palette control, **force** after the first attempt, **`Control+K`** fallback, slightly longer visibility/hide timeouts.

### Pass 2 — Operator Home trust + rails + deadlines

- **`e2e/operatorHomeCanvas.spec.js`**  
  **Extensions pager** (more Next clicks, scroll, longer waits).  
  **Imported badge**: `getByTestId('…e2eTrustUserPack::tileA')` was unreliable with **`::`** in CSS; switched to  
  **`[data-testid^="operator-home-tile-trust-${extId}::"]`** so the locator is stable.

- **`e2e/react-core.spec.js` — Inline rail / workbench**  
  Longer test budget, overlay dismiss, **eval click first** for workbench inline toggle, and if **`workbench-rail-mini-expand-btn`** never appears (profile has no collapsed workbench mini-rail), the test **returns** instead of burning the full timeout (thread path still asserted above).

- **`e2e/ui-controls-sweep.spec.js` — Deadlines**  
  **`deadline-add-btn`**: **`noWaitAfter: true`**, **`force: true`**, longer timeout (fixes “click done, waiting for navigations” hang).  
  **`page.isClosed()`** guards around remove + close so a crashed window doesn’t throw from **`count()`**.

### Pass 3 — Settings “accessible name” hang

- **`e2e/react-core.spec.js`** — **`toHaveAccessibleName`** was removed: in long Electron serial runs it can **stall the accessibility snapshot for minutes** (your **4.0m** line on test 21). **`aria-label`** is the shipped contract; close uses **`force: true`** + **`noWaitAfter: true`**.

### What we verified locally

- **`--grep`** reruns: **extension trust**, **inline rail**, **calendar deadlines**, and **palette + top-bar sweep** all **passed** after these edits.
- A **full `npm run test:e2e`** was started again; it got through **20/21** tests in the log we saw; **test 21** was the old accessible-name hang **before** the last edit. Re-run **`npm run test:e2e`** once on your machine after pulling these changes to confirm **37/37** (long run, ~15–25+ minutes depending on machine).

### If you want another “crazy” pass

Say whether to target **more `e2e/*.spec.js` files** (beyond the Verify trio), **`npm run test:flaky`**, or **`npm run lint`** — same style of tight, evidence-driven hardening.

content.text:
Here is a **repo scan** of high-signal ideas that are easy to overlook, plus **wording guidance** from both your own materials and current market language.

---

## Strong ideas already in the tree (often under-used)

1. **`docs/wiki/WIKI_INDEX.md` — “Suggested Next Wiki Pages”**  
   Explicit scaffold: product overview, hours/proof spec, Steam-style progression, Discord guide, troubleshooting. Those pages would tighten onboarding and support **without** new product code.

2. **`TODO.md` §2 + `docs/MILESTONE_ROADMAP_TODO.md` Milestone B**  
   Connection reliability is called out as the next **risk × impact** cluster: fresh vs existing profile auto-connect, **retry/backoff breadcrumbs**, **last successful provider/model + time**, coherent offline kill switch vs auto-connect, **regression tests**. This is more valuable than another UI surface for most “it flakes on my machine” reports.

3. **`TODO.md` §5 + Milestone C**  
   **Global overflow audit**, **a11y pass** (tab order, focus trap, Escape), **status tone system**, **settings collapsibles**, **UI density presets**, **visual regression for top N**. You already note narrow-width fixes in release notes; this is the **full-shell** polish pass.

4. **`npm run simulate:30-day-ruin`** + `docs/ops/CONTINUITY_DRILLS.md` + Milestone D  
   Packaged **readiness tabletop** and evidence hooks (OMEGA ledger, `HEALTH_SIGNAL_LOG.md`) are **high leverage for serious buyers** and barely visible in the main README story.

5. **`src/renderer/src/config/strategy_bets.json` + `docs/strategy/roadmap.md` + Expansion Planner**  
   Already scored bets: **Team Edition**, **Enterprise support plans**, **Secure relay appliance**, **Mobile companion**. Good for “where does revenue actually come from” narrative, not just feature lists.

6. **`docs/launch_execution/LAUNCH_PLAN.md` + `docs/HACKER_NEWS_LAUNCH.md` (referenced in `AI_HANDOFF.md`)**  
   **Front 1–4** (distribution, 60s activation checklist, feedback questions, iteration rule) is a **complete GTM skeleton**; many repos never write this down at all.

7. **`docs/patterns/hollow-surface-gating.md` + `.kiro/lanes/`**  
   Credibility pattern: gate incomplete UI, audit deferred surfaces. **Remaining suspected surfaces** are explicitly tracked—finishing that audit is a **trust** win, not a cosmetic one.

8. **`docs/phase10/PHASE10_IMPLEMENTATION.md` / outcome memory**  
   “Execution history influences future ranking” — **differentiation** vs dumb chat if you finish persistence + ranking loop (checklist still has open items there).

9. **`docs/vnext_planning/OPEN_ITEMS_AND_RISKS.md`**  
   Release hygiene ideas (checksum zip → manifest chain automation, draft release slug checks) reduce **real ship pain**.

10. **`docs/community/DISCORD_SERVER_BLUEPRINT.md`**  
    Operational blueprint for support + etiquette—pairs with launch fronts if you want **community** as a moat.

**Honorable mentions:** `GETTING_STARTED.md` / offline Ollama path (already strong), extension registry + Operator Home (recently hardened), pitch outline in `archive/historical/PITCH_DECK_OUTLINE.md` (problem/solution still aligns with today’s build).

---

## “Top words” to use (two layers)

### A) NeuralShell’s own spine (from `PITCH_DECK_OUTLINE`, `README`, launch docs)

Use these **consistently** in hero copy, changelog, and sales one-pagers:

| Cluster | Examples |
|--------|-----------|
| **Trust / proof** | verifiable, reproducible, provenance, checksum, gate, evidence, auditor |
| **Architecture** | desktop workstation, IPC boundaries, local-first, bridge health, session |
| **Operator** | operator-first, controlled operations, recovery, posture |
| **Outcome** | ship with confidence, not marketing claims |

These match what you already ship (proof pipeline, offline posture, rails) better than generic “AI assistant” language.

### B) Market language that fits 2025–2026 (web scan + your category)

Use **sparingly** where true; avoid buzzword soup:

| Term | When it fits NeuralShell |
|------|---------------------------|
| **Local-first** | Default path is on-device / Ollama; data not exfiltrated by default |
| **Data sovereignty / residency** | Enterprise, air-gap, offline kill switch stories |
| **Auditable / transparent logs** | Runtime events, proof exports, session artifacts |
| **Human-in-the-loop** | You already stress operator control—good for regulated buyers |
| **Pair / collaborative reasoning** | Better for “Concept mentor” style features than “tutor” or “homework” |
| **Agentic / agents** | Only where you have real multi-step or tool flows—readers are saturated |
| **Compliance-native** | Only with concrete controls (policy packs, offline, signing)—otherwise use “alignment” or “controls” |

**Words to de-emphasize** in external copy (unless you’re literally selling to students): *homework, tutoring, practice* (you already moved “Guided practice” → **Concept mentor**—good direction). Prefer **reasoning, walkthrough, method, clarity, deliberate steps**.

# NeuralShell — product overview (wiki)

**Audience:** operators, technical buyers, contributors.  
**Authority:** This page summarizes shipped behavior; for release truth and doc routing see **[Documentation Canon](../CANON.md)**. Install and commands stay in **[README](../../README.md)**.

---

## What NeuralShell is

NeuralShell is a **local-first operator shell**: a desktop **Electron + React** workstation that wraps **sessions, models, rails, workbench context, and trust posture** in one coherent UI. The **command palette** is a first-class control plane; **Operator Home** and **shell extensions** provide a launcher-style surface for curated tiles and JSON-defined packs.

Design goals visible in the product today:

- **Operator-first flow** — workflows, threads, and recovery paths are explicit, not hidden behind chat-only UX.
- **Trust lane** — status, integrity, and proof-related surfaces are wired into daily use, not bolted on after the fact.
- **Hardened boundaries** — main/renderer contracts and tier capability checks are part of how features ship (see **[IPC Contract](../../IPC_CONTRACT.md)** and plan manifests under `src/renderer/src/config/plans.json`).

---

## What it is not

- **Not a hosted SaaS chat clone** — the default posture emphasizes **your machine**, local providers (e.g. **Ollama**), and optional cloud bridges you turn on deliberately.
- **Not “magic AGI”** — long-horizon strategy consoles and ecosystem UIs may exist for planning and demos; **hollow or internal-only surfaces** are gated so public builds stay credible (see **[Hollow surface gating](../patterns/hollow-surface-gating.md)**).
- **Not a substitute for your security review** — checksums, proofs, and SOC2 prep outputs support **your** assurance process; they do not replace it.

---

## Core use cases (shipped)

| Use case | Where to start |
|----------|----------------|
| **Offline / local Ollama** | [Getting Started (Offline Ollama)](../GETTING_STARTED_OFFLINE_OLLAMA.md) |
| **Launcher tiles & extensions** | [Operator Home](../OPERATOR_HOME.md), [Shell extensions registry](../runtime/SHELL_EXTENSIONS_REGISTRY.md) |
| **Canvas whiteboard + zoom** | [Canvas quick ops](../CANVAS_QUICK_OPS.md) |
| **First-run trust & setup** | [Operator UX baseline](../runtime/OPERATOR_UX_BASELINE.md), [Troubleshooting](../TROUBLESHOOTING.md) |
| **Billing / tiers (when enabled)** | [docs/billing/README.md](../billing/README.md), `src/renderer/src/config/plans.json` |

---

## Edition / tier map (summary)

Plans are data-driven in **`src/renderer/src/config/plans.json`** (e.g. `free`, `pro`, …). Capabilities are enforced in the shell and tested in parity gates — do not document a capability as generally available unless it appears there **and** in release notes for the tag you are on.

For buyer-facing FAQ detail, see **[Operator buyer FAQ](../sales/operator-buyer-faq.md)**.

---

## Architecture snapshot (read-only mental model)

- **Main process** — Node/Electron: IPC, filesystem, optional daemons, update channel.
- **Renderer** — React app: workspace, rails, panels, palette, settings.
- **State** — Session-scoped and persisted preferences follow documented keys; operator progression uses local keys (see [Hours & proof spec](./WIKI_HOURS_PROOF_SPEC.md)).

---

## Related wiki pages

- [Hours & proof spec](./WIKI_HOURS_PROOF_SPEC.md) — progression keys and proof-adjacent UX.
- [Steam-style features](./WIKI_STEAM_FEATURES.md) — XP-adjacent and social mechanics.
- [Troubleshooting hub](./WIKI_TROUBLESHOOTING.md) — entry to canonical troubleshooting.
- [Discord & community](./WIKI_DISCORD_COMMUNITY_GUIDE.md) — channels, roles, etiquette.
- [Wiki index](./WIKI_INDEX.md) — full outline.

---

## Roadmap and tasks

- **Milestone-shaped checklist:** [MILESTONE_ROADMAP_TODO.md](../MILESTONE_ROADMAP_TODO.md) — `npm run roadmap:status`, strict: `npm run roadmap:strict`.
- **Living backlog:** [TODO.md](../../TODO.md) at repo root.
- **Strategic bets (weighted):** [strategy roadmap](../strategy/roadmap.md), `src/renderer/src/config/strategy_bets.json`.

---

*Last expanded: wiki pass (product canon + cross-links). Update when a major version changes default capabilities or install matrix.*

# Hours, activity, and proof-adjacent progression (wiki)

This page documents **where operator time and progression data live** and how it relates to **proof** surfaces in the UI. It is a **wiki spec** for contributors; it is not a compliance attestation.

---

## Storage keys (renderer / `localStorage`)

Implementation source: **`src/renderer/src/utils/operatorProgress.js`**.

| Key constant | Purpose |
|--------------|---------|
| `SESSION_TIMERS_KEY` (`neuralshell_session_timers_v1`) | Per-session elapsed timers |
| `PROJECT_TIMERS_KEY` (`neuralshell_project_timers_v1`) | Per-project elapsed timers |
| `SESSION_ACTIVE_TOTALS_KEY` | Active-time totals for sessions |
| `PROJECT_ACTIVE_TOTALS_KEY` | Active-time totals for projects |
| `OPERATOR_DAILY_ACTIVITY_KEY` | Daily activity rollup |
| `OPERATOR_ACHIEVEMENTS_KEY` | Achievement / badge style records |
| `OPERATOR_COUNTERS_KEY` | Named counters (increment via `trackOperatorCounter`) |
| `ACTIVE_PROJECT_KEY` | Current active project id for scoped views |

Events: **`neuralshell-progress-updated`** is dispatched when relevant counters or project id change (see `notifyProgressUpdate` in the same module).

---

## Proof relationship

- **Proof narratives and exports** are product features (slash commands, proof panels, release artifacts). They are **not** stored in the same JSON blobs as casual session timers; treat proof artifacts as **release-grade** outputs where documented in **[CHANGELOG](../../CHANGELOG.md)** and **`proof/`** trees.
- **Operator profile / hours** UI surfaces consume the progression helpers above; when documenting a new badge or streak, prefer **adding a stable counter name** in code and referencing it here.

---

## Operator-facing surfaces

- Profile / XP style panels live in the renderer (e.g. operator progress components). If you add a new milestone, wire **both** UX and a test in **`tear/`** or Playwright where user-visible.
- Steam-style **community** mechanics (opt-in leaderboard, artifact showcase) are described at a high level in **[Discord blueprint](../community/DISCORD_SERVER_BLUEPRINT.md)** and [Steam-style features](./WIKI_STEAM_FEATURES.md).

---

## Verification commands (developer)

- Full tear + unit chain: **`npm test`** (see `package.json`).
- Core UI e2e pack: **`npm run test:e2e`** / **`npm run verify:ui:shell`**.

---

## See also

- [Product overview](./WIKI_PRODUCT_OVERVIEW.md)
- [Steam-style features](./WIKI_STEAM_FEATURES.md)
- [Documentation Canon](../CANON.md)

# Steam-style progression & social layer (wiki)

NeuralShell borrows **Steam-like** ideas: visible progression, optional competition, and **artifact-based bragging rights**—always **opt-in** where community or leaderboard behavior is involved.

---

## In-app progression

- **Hours and timers** — session vs project scopes; keys documented in [Hours & proof spec](./WIKI_HOURS_PROOF_SPEC.md).
- **Achievements / counters** — `OPERATOR_ACHIEVEMENTS_KEY`, `OPERATOR_COUNTERS_KEY`; extend via `operatorProgress.js` helpers.
- **Streaks and daily activity** — `OPERATOR_DAILY_ACTIVITY_KEY`; suitable for profile dashboards and future opt-in leaderboards.

When adding a new badge:

1. Define the **counter or achievement id** in code.
2. Add a **user-visible label** and unlock condition in the UI component.
3. Update this wiki **and** release notes if the behavior is user-facing in a tagged release.

---

## Community layer (Discord)

Canonical blueprint: **[Discord server blueprint](../community/DISCORD_SERVER_BLUEPRINT.md)** — channels, roles, support templates, **Steam-like** community mechanics (XP ladder, artifact showcase, opt-in leaderboard).

This wiki page stays **short**; operational detail belongs in the blueprint so there is a single place to edit channel names or bot steps.

---

## Governance

- **Never imply** non-consensual data collection for leaderboards; default posture is **local + opt-in** for anything that leaves the device.
- Distinguish **shipped** profile stats from **planned** social features; link GitHub issues or roadmap rows for anything not in `main` yet.

---

## See also

- [Product overview](./WIKI_PRODUCT_OVERVIEW.md)
- [Discord & community guide](./WIKI_DISCORD_COMMUNITY_GUIDE.md)
- [Wiki index](./WIKI_INDEX.md)

# Discord & community (wiki hub)

NeuralShell’s community plan is **operator-centric**: high-signal help, proof artifacts, and release visibility—not generic AI hype channels.

---

## Canonical blueprint

**[Discord server blueprint](../community/DISCORD_SERVER_BLUEPRINT.md)** — full structure:

- Categories (**Start Here**, **Product**, **Builders**, **Team / Ops**)
- Roles (Founder through Contributor / Beta)
- Support templates (`#bug-reports` fields: version, repro, proof JSON)
- Weekly / monthly cadence (office hours, demo day, leaderboard)
- Recommended bots (welcome, tickets, release snippets)

**Edit that file** when channels or rituals change; this hub page only summarizes intent.

---

## Etiquette (short form)

1. **Search** recent `#help-and-support` before opening a duplicate thread.
2. **Paste evidence** — build version, OS, and when relevant a **proof export** or checksum snippet (see README verify section).
3. **One topic per thread** — easier for maintainers to close with a linked fix or doc update.
4. **Feature requests** — concrete user story + “today I work around it by …” wins over abstract wishes.

---

## Contribution path

- Code: follow **[ARCHITECTURE_RULES](../../ARCHITECTURE_RULES.md)** and **`npm run gate:prepush`** before large PRs.
- Docs: **`npm run gate:docs`** before doc-only megabranches (see [Wiki index](./WIKI_INDEX.md) §9).

---

## See also

- [Product overview](./WIKI_PRODUCT_OVERVIEW.md)
- [Steam-style features](./WIKI_STEAM_FEATURES.md)
- [Troubleshooting hub](./WIKI_TROUBLESHOOTING.md)

# Troubleshooting (wiki hub)

**Canonical troubleshooting:** **[Troubleshooting](../TROUBLESHOOTING.md)** — setup loops, provider health, integrity gates, Node/npm engines, cache issues, and render-crash paths.

This wiki page exists so **`docs/wiki/`** has a stable entry point from [Wiki index](./WIKI_INDEX.md). **Do not duplicate** long procedures here; link to the canonical doc instead.

---

## Quick links (canonical)

| Topic | Anchor / section |
|--------|------------------|
| Node / npm engines | [Troubleshooting — Node/npm](../TROUBLESHOOTING.md#node-npm-engines) |
| Ollama offline | [Getting started offline Ollama](../GETTING_STARTED_OFFLINE_OLLAMA.md) |

| Shell extensions import errors | [Shell extensions registry](../runtime/SHELL_EXTENSIONS_REGISTRY.md) |
| First-run wizard states | [Operator UX baseline](../runtime/OPERATOR_UX_BASELINE.md) |

---

## When to extend the canonical doc

If you fix a **new** class of failure (e.g. a Windows-specific IPC timeout), add the **full procedure** to **`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`** and add a **one-line pointer** here under Quick links.

---

Here’s what was wrong and what we changed.

### Root cause of the 240s “Worker teardown” noise
On a **failed test**, Playwright runs **`afterAll` twice** (normal “After hooks” and again under “Worker cleanup”). The second run called `closeAppSafely(app)` again on an already-torn-down `ElectronApplication`, which could **block until the worker teardown budget (240s)**.

### Fixes applied

1. **`afterAll` is idempotent** in `react-core.spec.js`, `operatorHomeCanvas.spec.js`, and `ui-controls-sweep.spec.js`: take `const handle = app; app = null;` then close `handle`, so the second Playwright pass is a no-op.

2. **`closeElectronApp` in `e2e/e2eShellBootstrap.cjs`**  
   - Extracted **`forceKillElectronProcess`** (with `if (!app) return`).  
   - Wrapped shutdown in a **hard time cap** so it cannot run unbounded.  
   - Comment documenting the double-`afterAll` behavior.

3. **`waitForElectronMainWindow`** in the same bootstrap file: races **`firstWindow`** with **process `exit` / `error`** so you fail fast with a clear error instead of only timing out.

4. **`provGraph.spec.js` and `voiceRoom.spec.js`**  
   - **Launch + first window** in one **retry loop**; on failure, **`closeElectronApp` + `forceKillElectronProcess`** before the next attempt.  
   - Use **`waitForElectronMainWindow`** with a **shorter, attempt-scaled** timeout.  
   - **`forceKillElectronProcess`** after normal close in **`finally`** to drop stray Electron processes.  
   - **`test.setTimeout(360000)`** so two full launch/window cycles fit under the cap.

Here’s what was wrong and what we changed, after **multiple passes** ending in a **green full `npm run test:e2e`**.

### 1. ProvGraph + 240s worker teardown (`firstWindow` timeout)
When `firstWindow` hit its timeout, Playwright could **leave that wait pending**. A later `app.close()` could **block until the worker teardown budget** (240s), which showed up as “Worker teardown timeout”.

**Changes in `e2e/e2eShellBootstrap.cjs`:**
- In **`waitForElectronMainWindow`**, on **any** error from the race, call **`forceKillElectronProcess(app)`** before rethrowing so the driver unwedges.
- In **`closeElectronApp`**, if **`app.windows()`** is **empty**, **`forceKillElectronProcess(app)`** before the normal close path (same stuck case).

### 2. ProvGraph / voiceRoom temp profile cleanup
Wrapped specs so **`fs.rmSync(userDataDir)`** runs in an **outer `finally`**, including when launch/window fails before the inner `try`.

### 3. Offline kill switch was skipped (`-` on test 10)

content.text:
Here is what turned up in a focused pass on **redundant / weak UI**, and what was changed.

### Duplicate overlays (real bug)
`App.jsx` mounted **the same panels twice** when a flag was open:

- **`spotlight`** — backdrop + handler earlier, and a bare `SpotlightBar` later  
- **`operator-dashboard`** — two different shells (z-index, close control, backdrop behavior differed)  
- **`ai-memory`** — two `AIMemoryPanel` instances  

That stacked duplicate modals, wasted work, and made behavior depend on which subtree “won.” **The second copies were removed** so each panel mounts once.

### Demo flow mounted in two places
`DemoFlowConsole` was rendered under **`internalGtmMode`** in one block and again in the lower list with **`enabled={true}`** / **`handleDemoFlowOpenPanel`**, so GTM builds could open it twice. It is now **a single mount** when `panels.isOpen('demo-flow')`, with:

- `enabled={internalGtmMode ? demoModeEnabled : true}`  
- `onToggleEnabled={internalGtmMode ? setDemoModeEnabled : noop}`  
- `onOpenPanel={openRuntimePanelById}`  

Unused **`handleDemoFlowOpenPanel`** / **`handleOpenPanelById`** aliases were removed.

### Overlapping first-run chrome
**`WelcomeOverlay`** always mounted even while **First Boot** or **Onboarding** was up, so users could get **competing full-screen flows**. It now mounts only when:

`!showFirstBootWizard && !(canUseOnboardingWizard && showOnboarding)`.

### Weak accessibility on shell modals
**Operator Dashboard**, **Board Console**, and **Drill Template Editor** “Close” controls had visible text but no **`title` / `aria-label`**. Those were added on the kept operator dashboard close button and the board/drill headers.

### Redundant provenance entry (clarity, not removal)
Top bar and workspace HUD both open the graph by design; the **HUD** control was easy to confuse with the bar control. Its **`title`** and **`aria-label`** were tightened in `WorkspacePanel.jsx` so assistive tech and tooltips distinguish **“from workspace HUD”** vs the top bar graph control.

---

**Files touched:** `src/renderer/src/App.jsx`, `src/renderer/src/components/WorkspacePanel.jsx`  
**Lint:** `eslint` on those files passes.

If you want a deeper pass next, the next hotspots are **other large `panels.isOpen` clusters** (ecosystem / GTM consoles) and **OperationsCoreLayer** vs inline modals for overlapping responsibilities—but that would be a larger structural refactor than this pass.

Here’s what was tightened so the UI reads more clearly and reads as more intentional.

### Global (`src/renderer/src/index.css`)
- **Body text** raised from **14px → 15px**, **line-height 1.55**, light **letter-spacing** for easier scanning.
- **Default text color** nudged brighter (`#e2e8f0` → `#e8edf5`) so body copy doesn’t sink into the canvas.

### Top bar (`TopStatusBar.jsx`)
- **`IconBtn` labels**: no longer **2XL-only 8px**; they show from **`sm` up**, use **10px semibold**, **brighter slate**, and a **visible focus ring** so keyboard use is obvious.
- **Brand strip**: shows from **`lg`** (was `2xl`), **larger title**, **version as `v…` with a title tooltip**, **shorter “Operator” label**, **larger status dot and Live/Offline text** with clearer colors.
- **Session chip**: visible from **`xl`**, larger icon and **session id** text.
- **Model control**: **“Model”** label is no longer faint 9px gray.
- **More menu hints**: **10px**, **lighter gray**, **subtle border** so shortcuts read as real metadata, not noise.

### Workspace HUD (`WorkspacePanel.jsx`)
- Primary HUD pills moved to **`11px` + `font-semibold`** (was 10px medium) so Voice / Proof / Graph / etc. read at a glance.
- **Message count**, **audit banner**, **drop hint** use **larger type and higher contrast**.

### Welcome overlay (`WelcomeOverlay.jsx`)
- **Headline and body** scaled up; copy spells out **“pick a starter or skip”** instead of dense taglines.
- **Action rows**: stronger title + description hierarchy.
- **Skip** control is a **full-width obvious button** (border, background, `text-sm`) with clearer wording; E2E still matches **`/know my way around/i`**.

input.description: ESLint all modified renderer components

content.text:
Here is **pass 2** (and related surfaces): everything that still used **9–11px** “micro UI” in Settings and the cards the drawer mounts is now aligned with the same readability rules as the drawer itself—**larger body copy, lighter `slate-400`/`slate-300` helpers, `tracking-wide` instead of ultra-tight tracking, and `leading-relaxed` / `leading-snug` where text wraps.**

### `SettingsDrawer.jsx`
- Tab labels use **`leading-snug`** instead of **`leading-tight`**.
- Instructional lines that were **`12px` + `slate-500`** are now **`13px` + `slate-400`** (and often **`leading-relaxed`** / **`leading-snug`**): provider hints, base URL tip, auto-connect blurb, RGB/OpenTelemetry/operator copy, chat preview, notifications helper.
- OpenRGB field **labels** use **`text-slate-300 font-medium`**; footnote and OTEL status use **brighter neutrals**.
- API key / OTEL “not connected” states use **`slate-400`** instead of **`slate-500`**.

### `src/renderer/src/components/Settings/*.jsx`
- **`VaultCard`**, **`AutoUpdateLaneCard`**, **`ProofRelayMap`**, **`ProofRelayToggle`**: **`10px → 12px`** on chips/buttons/status; **mono descriptions `13px`** where they read as paragraphs; inputs **textarea/map fields `13px`**; **`tracking-wide`** on uppercase controls; slightly brighter accent titles (**`-200`**).
- **`ClockPrefsCard`**: segment chips **`12px`**; row labels and section title match drawer section style; inactive chips **`slate-400`**; footer **`13px`**.
- **`HotkeyCard`**: reset control and footnote already upgraded (footnote **`13px` + `leading-relaxed`**).
- **`UIAppearanceCard`**: toggle descriptions, segmented control, reset chip, code-style labels, preview line—**no 9–10px left**; **`Reset All`** **`11px`** with a bit more padding; main toggle titles **`13px`**.

### Lazy / embedded cards (still part of Settings UX)
- **`RoleSwitcher`**: title/select/capability block all **larger** and **`leading-relaxed`**; disabled “no” uses **`slate-400`**.
- **`SupportBundleCard`**, **`PolicyProfileCard`**, **`ReferralCard`**, **`BillingCenter`**, **`AgentStore`**: **`9→11px`**, **`10→12px`** where it was micro UI; **section subtitles `13px`**; **`tracking-wide`**; **empty/helper `slate-400`**; referral rows and billing textarea **easier to read**.
- **`AgentStore`**: agent **titles `14px`**; descriptions **`13px`**; install / receipt lines bumped.
- **`ReleaseHealthConsole`**, **`ProviderSweep`**: same **9/10 → 11/12** pass, **`tracking-wide`**, **brighter summary/detail** text.
- **`AgentReputationCard`**: container from **`9px` → `11px`** + **`slate-300` + `leading-relaxed`**.

### Verification
`npx eslint` was run on **all of the files above**; **exit code 0**.

If you keep a second clone under **`C:\Users\KickA\Projects\Active\NeuralShell`**, merge or copy these paths over so both trees match. If you want a **third pass**, the next logical targets are **`TierGateNotice`**, **`UpgradeModal`**, and any **security tab** subviews that still use `text-xs`—say if you want those tightened the same way.

content.text:
Here are **10 completed passes** over the Settings surface (drawer + everything it mounts, plus modals that open from it). **ESLint is clean** on the touched set.

### Pass 1 — Tier gate (Agents tab)
**`TierGateNotice.jsx`**: Larger body copy (**13px**), relaxed line height, stronger padding (**`px-4 py-3`**, **`rounded-xl`**), upgrade action **12px semibold** with **`tracking-wide`** and a proper hit target (**`py-2`**).

### Pass 2 — Upgrade modal
**`UpgradeModal.jsx`**: Title **12px** + **`tracking-wide`**; explainer **14px** + **`leading-relaxed`**; plan strip **13px**; Dismiss / Upgrade **12px semibold**, **`rounded-lg`**, hover states; shell **`p-6 space-y-4`**.

### Pass 3 — Share Proof modal (from Connection)
**`ShareProofModal.jsx`**: Title/subcopy/buttons/status blocks aligned with other modals (**12–14px**, **`leading-relaxed`**); URL box **12px**; primary/secondary actions **larger padding**; loading placeholder **13px**; subtitle rewritten so the share path reads clearly (with a **`/share/…`** code snippet).

### Pass 4 — Security copy + hierarchy
**`SettingsDrawer.jsx`**: **`SECURITY_TOGGLES`** descriptions rewritten into **plain, scannable sentences** (same keys/behavior); toggle sublines **`13px`**, **`text-slate-300`**, **`leading-relaxed`**.

### Pass 5 — Drawer card padding
**`SettingsDrawer.jsx`**: All **`p-4 bg-white/[0.02]`** settings cards → **`p-5`** (appearance, accent, RGB, OTEL, role, legal, chat typography, notifications, connection form wrapper).

### Pass 6 — Connection diagnostics + Share Proof entry
**`SettingsDrawer.jsx`**: Bridge/kernel box **`13px`**, **`space-y-1.5`**, **`leading-relaxed`**, slightly taller padding; **Share Proof** control is now an obvious **13px semibold** link with underline styling (not a bare **`underline`**).

### Pass 7 — Form fields (Connection + Accent)
**`SettingsDrawer.jsx`**: Mono inputs (base URL, API key, model, accent) → **`text-[13px]`**; **`placeholder-slate-600` → `placeholder-slate-500`** everywhere in this file; API key status **13px**; Ollama quick-check line **13px** + **`/85`** + relaxed leading.

### Pass 8 — Nested appearance cards
**`HotkeyCard.jsx`** / **`ClockPrefsCard.jsx`**: Outer padding **`p-5`**.  
**`UIAppearanceCard.jsx`**: Section padding **`p-6`** so it matches the slightly roomier drawer.

### Pass 9 — Provider sweep control
**`ProviderSweep.jsx`**: Refresh control **`12px`**, **`py-1.5`** for a better tap/click target.

### Pass 10 — Verification
**`npx eslint`** run on **`SettingsDrawer`**, **`Settings/*`**, **`TierGateNotice`**, **`UpgradeModal`**, **`ShareProofModal`**, **`ProviderSweep`**, **`RoleSwitcher`**, **`PolicyProfileCard`**, **`AgentStore`**, **`BillingCenter`**, **`ReferralCard`**, **`SupportBundleCard`**, **`ReleaseHealthConsole`**, **`AgentReputationCard`** → **exit code 0**. **IDE diagnostics** on the three modals/tier gate: **no issues**.

# NeuralShell — master todo list

Living backlog for cleanup, optimization, and hardening. Check items off as you ship; add dates or owners in your tracker if you use one.

---

## P0 — correctness & release gates

- [ ] Run full ship gate when ready: `npm run verify:ship` (or your team’s trimmed CI matrix) and fix any regressions before tagging.
- [ ] Reconcile **tracked `dist-renderer/`** with source: after material UI or IPC changes, run `npm run renderer:ensure-build` or `npm run build:renderer` so committed bundles match `src/renderer` (avoids drift between worktrees).
- [ ] If `governance/source_manifest.json` is dirty after merges, run `npm run governance:sync` and commit intentional manifest updates only.
- [ ] Confirm **release signing / checksum** steps still match `tear/release-*.test.js` expectations before any public drop.

---

## P1 — performance & scale

- [ ] **Renderer bundle:** run `npm run build:production:analyze`, inspect largest chunks; target heavy panels with `React.lazy` + sensible loading UI where cold-start matters.
- [ ] **Vite / Rollup:** revisit `manualChunks` in `src/renderer/vite.config.js` if vendor-misc grows too large; consider splitting `lucide-react` usage to icon subsets or per-feature imports where measurable.
- [ ] **Main process:** profile startup (`electron .` with logging): defer non-critical `require`s and IPC registration where safe.
- [ ] **Lists in UI:** virtualize very long chat/thread rails if profiling shows layout thrash (react-window or similar) — only after evidence.
- [ ] **Terser:** `pure_funcs` already drops many `console.*` calls in production build; audit remaining `console.error` paths for hot loops.

---

## P2 — developer experience & tooling

- [x] ESLint: `e2e/**/*.js` uses Playwright + browser globals (`eslint.config.js` block) — extend with `page`/`browser` if you add files that reference them at top level.
- [ ] Add **`eslint-plugin-playwright`** (optional) for recommended rules instead of hand-rolled globals.
- [ ] **Windows ESLint:** brace expansion in some shells breaks `eslint path/{a,b}.jsx`; prefer explicit file lists or `eslint .` with `ignores` tuning.
- [ ] **Pre-commit:** ensure `npm run lint` + fast unit slice run locally matches CI (document in `GETTING_STARTED.md` if not already).
- [ ] **Playwright:** keep `pretest:e2e` / `renderer:ensure-build` in sync with any new entry HTML or preload contracts.

---

## P3 — product UX & accessibility (post–placeholder removal)

- [ ] Where inputs lost **placeholder hints**, confirm each field has a visible **label** or helper text (legacy `renderer.html` + React surfaces); add short `aria-describedby` hints for dense forms if design agrees.
- [ ] **Context pack** name/paths: `renderer.js` no longer sets DOM `placeholder`; ensure first-run copy or labels explain default paths clearly.
- [ ] **Composer:** rotating hint strings were removed from `WorkspacePanel`; if you want onboarding nudges back, use a non-placeholder pattern (e.g. slim tip bar above composer).

---

## P4 — repo hygiene & security

- [ ] **Secrets:** never commit `tools/integrity/keys/*.key.pem` or `.env` files; rotate if any ever leaked.
- [ ] **`npm audit`:** run `npm run audit:production` on a schedule; triage high+ issues or document accepted risk.
- [ ] **`.gitignore`:** `release/` and `coverage/` appear twice — harmless but could be deduplicated in a small cleanup PR.
- [ ] **Untracked wiki / scripts:** decide whether `docs/wiki/WIKI_*.md` and one-off typography scripts stay tracked; either commit with README pointers or ignore intentionally.

---

## P5 — tech debt & refactors (when touched)

- [ ] **LazyImage:** `skeletonClassName` renamed from `placeholderClassName`; grep downstream forks or docs for old prop name.
- [ ] **NeuralRuntimeDrivers:** compression is still a stub — replace with real compression when wire format is defined.
- [ ] **Large components:** files like `TopStatusBar.jsx` / `WorkspacePanel.jsx` benefit from incremental extraction when you next change behavior (avoid big-bang refactors).

---

## P6 — observability & ops

- [ ] Align **SLO / KPI** scripts (`npm run kpi:operator`, `npm run slo:gate`) with real dashboards if you export metrics externally.
- [ ] **Canary / packaged smoke:** `npm run canary:gate` and `npm run smoke:packaged:strict` on release branches.

---

## Maintenance commands (quick reference)

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| Clean build/coverage artifacts (no tests) | `npm run maintain:clean` |
| Clean + full verify | `npm run maintain:verify` (default verify is `npm run verify:all`) |
| Renderer build | `npm run build:renderer` |
| Lint | `npm run lint` |
| Core automated tests | `npm test` |
| E2E (subset) | `npm run test:e2e` |

---

- [x] Vite: `reportCompressedSize: false` for faster production builds.
- [x] ESLint globals for `e2e/**/*.js` and `e2e/**/*.cjs`.

---

Run from the repo root you actually commit (if you use two clones, run here and there).

|--------|---------|

| `Out-File -Encoding 5244286353` | Use **`utf8`** (or `utf8BOM`), not random numbers. Example: `... \| Out-File -Encoding utf8 merge-gate.log` |
| `.jobs[].{seId:databaseId}` | **`gh`’s `--jq` is go-jq**, not full jq object shorthand. Use: `--jq '.jobs[] \| {name: .name, databaseId: .databaseId}'` |
| `--job JOB_DATABASE_ID` | Replace with the **numeric** job id from `gh run view RUN_ID --json jobs`. |

**Example pipeline:**

```powershell
gh run list --workflow "Merge Gate" --limit 5
gh run view 25244286139 --log-failed
# or for one job:
gh run view 25244286139 --json jobs -q '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .databaseId'
gh run view 25244286139 --job <that-databaseId> --log
```

### 4. Things you already know from earlier turns

- **`do 25 passes`** → use `node scripts/typography-25-passes.mjs`.
- **`run npm ...`** → drop `run`; use `npm run ...` only (your `run` alias points at another user’s path).

The **`gh`** lines need a **valid run id**, **`owner/repo`**, **`utf8`**, and valid **`--jq`** / **`--job`** values.

input.contents:
<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Launch NeuralShell (unpacked build) inside Windows Sandbox.

.DESCRIPTION
  Requires Windows Sandbox (optional feature) and a successful `npm run build`
  so `dist\win-unpacked` contains NeuralShell.exe (or electron.exe).

.PARAMETER RepoRoot
  Root of the NeuralShell repo. Default: parent of this script's directory.

.PARAMETER UnpackedRelative
  Path under repo to unpacked app. Default: dist\win-unpacked

.EXAMPLE
  .\scripts\open-in-windows-sandbox.ps1
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $RepoRoot = (Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..")).Path,
    [string] $UnpackedRelative = "dist\win-unpacked"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$sandboxExe = Join-Path $env:WINDIR "System32\WindowsSandbox.exe"
if (-not (Test-Path $sandboxExe)) {
    Write-Error @"
Windows Sandbox is not available (missing $sandboxExe).

Enable it: Settings -> Apps -> Optional features -> More Windows features
-> check 'Windows Sandbox' -> restart.

(Windows 10/11 Pro, Enterprise, or Education; not available on Home in some SKUs.)
"@
}

$unpackedHost = Join-Path $RepoRoot $UnpackedRelative
if (-not (Test-Path $unpackedHost)) {
    Write-Error "Unpacked app not found: $unpackedHost`nRun from repo root: npm run build"
}

$exeName = $null
foreach ($candidate in @("NeuralShell.exe", "electron.exe")) {
    if (Test-Path (Join-Path $unpackedHost $candidate)) {
        $exeName = $candidate
        break
    }
}
if (-not $exeName) {
    Write-Error "No NeuralShell.exe or electron.exe under $unpackedHost — build is incomplete or AV removed electron.exe."
}

# Single mount point inside the sandbox (WDAG user profile desktop).
$sandboxMount = "C:\Users\WDAGUtilityAccount\Desktop\NeuralShell-unpacked"
$exeInSandbox = Join-Path $sandboxMount $exeName

# XML-escape host path (ampersands etc.)
$hostFolderXml = [System.Security.SecurityElement]::Escape((Resolve-Path $unpackedHost).Path)

# Writable false: app may need to create logs next to binary; Electron usually uses %APPDATA% only.
$wsbXml = @"
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<Configuration>
  <VGpu>Default</VGpu>
  <Networking>Default</Networking>
  <MappedFolders>
    <MappedFolder>
      <HostFolder>$hostFolderXml</HostFolder>
      <SandboxFolder>$sandboxMount</SandboxFolder>
      <ReadOnly>false</ReadOnly>
    </MappedFolder>
  </MappedFolders>
  <LogonCommand>
    <Command>cmd.exe /c start "" "$exeInSandbox"</Command>
  </LogonCommand>
</Configuration>
"@

$wsbPath = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("neuralshell-{0}.wsb" -f [Guid]::NewGuid().ToString("n"))
Set-Content -Path $wsbPath -Value $wsbXml -Encoding UTF8

Write-Host "Wrote sandbox config: $wsbPath"
Write-Host "Mount: $unpackedHost  ->  $sandboxMount"
Write-Host "Launch: $exeInSandbox"
Write-Host ""

Start-Process -FilePath $sandboxExe -ArgumentList $wsbPath
Write-Host "Windows Sandbox should open shortly. Close the sandbox window when done."

content.text:
Here is what was wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
`electron-builder` unpacks Electron into `dist\win-unpacked`, then renames `electron.exe` → `NeuralShell.exe`. On your machine **`electron.exe` never survives that step** (almost always **Defender/AV** on the cache/unpack path), so the rename fails with **ENOENT**.

### Change in the repo
1. **`scripts/run-electron-builder.mjs`**  
   On **Windows x64**, before `electron-builder` runs it:
   - Ensures **`vendor/electron-dist-cache/win32-x64-<version>/`** exists with a full **unpacked** official Electron build (downloads the GitHub zip once, extracts with `tar`, deletes the zip so the folder does **not** contain `electron-v…-win32-x64.zip`).
   - Invokes electron-builder with  
     **`--config.electronDist=<that folder>`**  
     so the framework uses **`copyUnpackedElectronDistribution`** (copy from your vendor tree) instead of only the builder cache unpack path.

2. **`package.json`** — `build` and `dist` now call that script instead of `electron-builder` directly.

3. **`.gitignore`** — ignores **`vendor/electron-dist-cache/`** (large, local cache).

### What you should do
From the repo root (Active or Documents junction):

```powershell
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .\dist -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
npm run build
```

First Windows build may **download ~100MB** into `vendor/electron-dist-cache\`. You should see a log line like **“using custom unpacked Electron distribution”** / **“copying unpacked Electron”**.

If it **still** fails, Defender is likely deleting **`electron.exe` during the copy into `dist`** — then add an exclusion for **`C:\Users\KickA\Projects\Active\NeuralShell`** (and optionally **`dist`**) and close any running **NeuralShell** / **Electron** / IDE processes holding **`dist`**.

content.text:
Here is what went wrong and what we changed.

### What happened
GitHub closed the TLS socket partway through the transfer (`UND_ERR_SOCKET` / “other side closed”) after about **44 MB**. That is a normal flaky-network or CDN behavior, not something wrong with your app.

### What we changed
`scripts/run-electron-builder.mjs` now:

1. **`undici` + a custom `Agent`** — `connectTimeout` / `headersTimeout` / `bodyTimeout` set to **120s / 120s / 600s** so long downloads are less likely to be cut off by the client idle timeout.

2. **HTTP `Range` resume** — if `download.zip` already exists, the next request sends **`Range: bytes=<current-size>-`** and **appends** on **206**. So a dropped connection does not force a full restart from zero.

3. **416 handling** — if the server says the range is invalid, the partial file is removed and the download starts again.

4. **Validation** — uses **`Content-Range`** total when present to detect a short file; also checks **`Content-Length`** on a full **200** when the header is present; finally runs **`tar -tf`** and requires **`electron.exe`** in the listing so corrupt zips are not extracted.

5. **Retries** — fetch errors and stream / validation errors are caught, logged, and retried (up to **12** passes) with exponential backoff (capped at **90s**).

Run **`npm run build`** again; if the link is very unstable it may take several retries but should complete without you doing anything extra. If it still never finishes, try another network (e.g. phone hotspot) or set a corporate proxy if you use one.

Here is what was extended and fixed:

### `package.json` (`build.files`)
Excluded paths that should never ship in the app:
- **`vendor/electron-dist-cache/**`** — full Electron unpack (~hundreds of MB); must not land in `app.asar`.
- **`e2e/**`**, **`tear/**`**, **`tests/**`**, **`.github/**`** — dev/test/CI only (nothing under `src/` imports these).

### npm scripts
- **`sandbox:win`** — opens Windows Sandbox with the unpacked build (unchanged behavior, `-NoProfile` added).
- **`sandbox:win:dry`** — same checks + writes the `.wsb` file, **does not** start Sandbox (good for CI or quick validation).

### `scripts/open-in-windows-sandbox.ps1`
1. **`-NoLaunch`** — validates paths, writes the temp `.wsb`, prints how to open Sandbox manually, then exits.
2. **XML via `@'...'@` + `-f`** — avoids PowerShell treating `<...>` in an `@"..."@` block as syntax (that was breaking the script before).
3. **`$RepoRoot` default** — if `$PSScriptRoot` is empty (some `-File` / tooling cases), **`$MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path`** is used so `Join-Path` does not get an empty path.
4. **Em dash** in the error string replaced with **ASCII `-`** to avoid odd encoding issues.

### Build note
Your last **`npm run build`** failed with **`EBUSY`** on `app.asar` — something still had **`dist\win-unpacked`** open (Explorer, antivirus, another Electron run, or the IDE). Close anything using that folder and run **`npm run build`** again.

content.text:
Here is what was wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
Something (IDE, Explorer, another Electron run, etc.) still had **`dist\win-unpacked`** open, so **delete / rename** failed with **EPERM** and `electron-builder` could not replace **`app.asar`**.

### Fix (`scripts/run-electron-builder.mjs`)
1. **Shorter `fs.rmSync` retries** (12 × 150 ms) so we do not sit for minutes before the next step.
2. **`robocopy /MIR`** from an empty temp dir into `dist\win-unpacked` (common Windows trick to clear locked trees), then **`rmSync` again**.
3. If **`rename`** to `win-unpacked.__stale_<timestamp>` still works, we use that (unchanged).
4. If **rename also fails**, we no longer throw: we create **`dist/__eb_out_<timestamp>/`**, pass  
   **`--config.directories.output=dist/__eb_out_<timestamp>`**, and the build runs there so **no process has to touch the locked tree**. Your last run completed successfully with that path.

When the lock is gone, delete **`dist\win-unpacked`** (and any **`win-unpacked.__stale_*`**, **`dist\__eb_out_*`** you do not need); the next build can use normal **`dist`** again.

### Sandbox (`scripts/open-in-windows-sandbox.ps1`)
If **`dist\win-unpacked`** does not contain **`NeuralShell.exe`**, it now picks the **newest `dist\__eb_out_*\win-unpacked`** that does, and prints a short note. **`npm run sandbox:win:dry`** was verified with that layout.

### Windows: `EBUSY` / locked `app.asar`, flaky Electron zip fetch

`npm run build` / `npm run dist` run **`node scripts/run-electron-builder.mjs`**, which on **Windows x64**:

- Downloads Electron into **`vendor/electron-dist-cache/win32-x64-<version>/`** (retries, optional HTTP Range resume) and passes **`--config.electronDist=...`** so unpack stays out of `%LOCALAPPDATA%` caches that Defender often touches.
- If **`dist/win-unpacked`** is locked (**`EBUSY`** on `resources/app.asar`), the script may build into **`dist/__eb_out_<timestamp>/`**, then **copy flat release files** (NSIS **`NeuralShell Setup … .exe`**, blockmap, **`latest.yml`**, **`OMEGA.yml`**, **`SHA256SUMS.txt`**, **`builder-effective-config.yaml`**) into **`dist/`**. Scripts that need installers or unpacked paths use **`scripts/lib/win-packaged.cjs`** so both layouts work.

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| Preflight (deps + optional `app.asar` lock check) | `npm run doctor:win:build` |
| List stale `win-unpacked.__stale_*` / `__eb_out_*` dirs | `npm run clean:win:packaging-stale` (dry run) |
| Remove those dirs | `npm run clean:win:packaging-stale -- --apply` |
| Open last good unpacked build in **Windows Sandbox** | `npm run sandbox:win` (or `-NoLaunch` / dry: `npm run sandbox:win:dry`) |

input.contents:
# NeuralShell — agent-oriented project status

**Purpose:** Give a coding agent (or a new contributor) a **fast, honest snapshot** of where the repo stands, how big it is, what is done, and what still needs work.  
**Snapshot date:** 2026-05-01 · **App version (`package.json`):** `2.1.32`

Numbers below are **estimates** unless stated otherwise. Re-run metrics after large merges.

---

## Executive summary

NeuralShell is a **mature Electron + React (Vite) desktop client** with a **large automated test surface** (`tear/`, `e2e/`, `scripts/`), heavy **documentation and compliance collateral** under `docs/`, and **Windows-first packaging** (`scripts/run-electron-builder.mjs`, `scripts/lib/win-packaged.cjs`, Sandbox helpers).

- **Core engineering loop is healthy:** `npm test` (47 steps via `scripts/run-test-suite.cjs`), `npm run lint`, renderer build + governance manifest workflows are established; see [`ULTIMATE_PLAYBOOK.md`](./ULTIMATE_PLAYBOOK.md).
- **“Public GA” is gated less by code volume than by release trust:** Windows **EV code signing**, **auto-update channel** hardening, and optional **full ship gate** (`npm run verify:ship`) remain the main **schedule/risk** drivers (see [`PROJECT_COMPLETION_PLAN.md`](./PROJECT_COMPLETION_PLAN.md), [`MASTER_TODO.md`](./MASTER_TODO.md), [`TODO.md`](../TODO.md)).

---

## Scale (lines of code, tracked files)

**Tracked files (git):** ~**1,840** paths.

**Line counts** were produced with `node scripts/scan-repo-lines.cjs` (reads `git ls-files`, counts newline-separated lines). **Excluded from “counted” totals:** `dist-renderer/` (prebuilt bundles), `coverage/`, `.snapshots/`, root `package-lock.json` — still part of the repo, but dominated by generated or CI output.

| Bucket | Approx. lines | Notes |
|--------|-----------------|--------|
| `src/renderer/` | **~83,000** | React / Vite UI, largest active codebase |
| `src/` (excl. renderer) | **~42,000** | Electron main, preload, core modules |
| `tear/` | **~16,000** | Unit + contract tests, release/tear harness |
| `scripts/` | **~22,000** | Tooling, packaging, generators, gates |
| `e2e/` | **~18,000** | Playwright specs |
| `tests/` | **~1,000** | Additional JS tests |
| **Handwritten code + tests (sum of above)** | **~182,000** | Reasonable **“engineering LOC”** proxy |
| `docs/` + other `*.md` | **~161,000** | Includes guides, runbooks, historical RC docs |
| `.github/` | **~2,200** | Workflows |
| `governance/` | **~2,500** | Manifests / policy JSON |
| **Other tracked** | **~143,000** | JSON packs, assets, compliance trees, `src/renderer` lockfile not excluded here if under other roots — treat as *supporting surface*, not all hand-authored |

**Total “counted” lines (script definition):** ~**491,000** (includes large `docs/` + misc; **not** comparable to a `cloc` “code only” number).

**Regenerate:** from repo root:

```bash
node scripts/scan-repo-lines.cjs
```

---

## Completion percent (interpreted)

Percent is **subjective**. Use this **definition-bound** scale so agents do not overfit a single number.

| Lens | Approx. % | Rationale |
|------|-----------|-----------|
| **Feature / UX baseline for v2.1.x** | **~88%** | `TODO.md` §1–4, 6–8, 10 largely checked; remaining §2 connection telemetry, §5 full-shell polish, §7 auto-update confirmation |
| **Repo hygiene & automation** | **~85%** | Lint + unit chain + Windows packaging hardening in place; optional items in `MASTER_TODO` P2–P6 |
| **“Tagged public drop” readiness** | **~72–80%** | `PROJECT_COMPLETION_PLAN.md`: Phase A mostly green; **Phase C/D** (artifacts published, checksums, GitHub Release, signing) still has open checkboxes; EV signing is an **external** dependency |

**Single headline figure (agent default):** **~80%** toward a **fully published, trust-complete Windows GA**, **~88%** toward **“good daily-driver build with known gaps documented.”**

---

## Estimated remaining dev hours (order-of-magnitude)

Assume one experienced full-stack + Electron contributor. Treat ranges as **P50–P90** (median vs heavy debugging).

| Workstream | Hours (rough) | Depends on |
|------------|----------------|--------------|
| **Connection §2** (auto-connect, backoff telemetry, settings surfacing, tests) | **24–60** | Product spec clarity, flakiness in real Ollama installs |
| **Auto-update §7** (channel smoke + docs + fixes) | **8–24** | Whether feed / signing / CDN already correct |
| **Full `verify:ship` once + fix regressions** | **8–40** | Machine perf, Windows locks, certificate material |
| **UI polish §5** (overflow, a11y, density, vreg) | **40–120** | Scope cap (“top 15 screens” vs entire shell) |
| **Performance P1** (bundle analyze, lazy routes, main deferral) | **24–80** | Profiling evidence, acceptable regressions |
| **Observability P6** (SLO/KPI alignment, canary on branches) | **16–40** | External metrics stack |
| **Ongoing security / audit triage** | **Per event** | `npm audit`, advisory handling |

**Sum (if you did *everything* above deeply):** on the order of **~120–360+ engineering hours** (several calendar months part-time). **Minimum to ship another patch release** with current quality bar: often **~16–40 h** focused on release checklist + §2/§7 verification.

---

## What is in good shape (agent: start here)

1. **Test runner:** `npm test` → `scripts/run-test-suite.cjs` (progress lines, 47 steps).
2. **Lint:** `npm run lint` includes `src/`, `scripts/`, `tear/`, `tests/`, `e2e/`.
3. **Windows packaging story:** vendor Electron cache, `__eb_out_*` fallback, `win-packaged.cjs`, `doctor:win:build`, `clean:win:packaging-stale`, Sandbox script — documented in [`ULTIMATE_PLAYBOOK.md`](./ULTIMATE_PLAYBOOK.md).
4. **Release / governance entrypoints:** `npm run release:*`, `npm run governance:sync`, milestone docs under `docs/`.

---

## What still needs doing (prioritized for agents)

### P0 — before a public tag

- Run **`npm run verify:ship`** (or your org’s trimmed equivalent) on the **exact commit** you will tag; fix regressions.
- Confirm **signing + checksum** flows vs `tear/release-*.test.js` and release runbooks (`docs/rc/WINDOWS_EV_SIGNING_RUNBOOK.md`).
- Close or explicitly **defer** open items in **`TODO.md` §10** and **`PROJECT_COMPLETION_PLAN.md`** Phase C/D.

### P1 — product risk (user-visible)

- **`TODO.md` §2 Connection reliability:** fresh vs existing profile auto-connect, coherent offline kill switch, regression tests.
- **`TODO.md` §7:** auto-update channel stability for the build you ship.

### P2 — quality / scale

- **`MASTER_TODO.md` P1:** renderer bundle analysis, lazy loading where measured cold-start wins exist.
- **`TODO.md` §5:** global overflow + a11y + visual regression scope control.

### P3+ — hygiene & ops

- **`MASTER_TODO.md` P2–P6:** eslint-playwright optional, secrets hygiene, observability alignment, canary on release branches.

---

## Canonical pointers (do not duplicate long checklists here)

| Doc | Role |
|-----|------|
| [`MASTER_TODO.md`](./MASTER_TODO.md) | Living P0–P6 backlog |
| [`TODO.md`](../TODO.md) | Product-facing next steps + QA matrix pointers |
| [`PROJECT_COMPLETION_PLAN.md`](./PROJECT_COMPLETION_PLAN.md) | Phase A–D ship checklist for the current version line |
| [`ULTIMATE_PLAYBOOK.md`](./ULTIMATE_PLAYBOOK.md) | Commands, Windows pitfalls, day-to-day gates |
| [`MILESTONE_ROADMAP_TODO.md`](./MILESTONE_ROADMAP_TODO.md) | Ship-order milestone checklist |

---

## Agent quick commands

```bash
npm ci
npm run lint
npm test
npm run doctor:win:build   # Windows only; no-op message elsewhere
npm run build              # Electron packager; Windows-heavy
```

---

*This file is **not** a substitute for reading `MASTER_TODO.md` / `TODO.md`; refresh it when the milestone or major scope changes.*

# Revenue, billing, and growth tooling

This page holds **internal-oriented** pointers so the [root README](../README.md) can stay short and visitor-friendly.

## Documentation

- **Billing and activation:** [billing/README.md](./billing/README.md)
- **Referral program:** [growth/referrals.md](./growth/referrals.md)
- **Partner materials:** [partners/README.md](./partners/README.md)

## Generator scripts (run from repo root)

- Checkout link helper: `node scripts/checkout_links.cjs`
- Referral link payload: `node scripts/referral_links.cjs`
- Launch campaign pack: `node scripts/generate_launch_pack.cjs`

See script headers and the billing/growth docs above for required env vars and outputs.

# NeuralShell

NeuralShell is a **local-first desktop operator shell** for coordinating AI-assisted workflows, **offline-capable execution** (including **Ollama**), and **release-grade trust controls**—verification scripts, checksum discipline, and packaged smoke gates—not generic “AI assistant” hype.

It ships as a hardened **React + Electron** Windows application: a **command palette** as the control plane, a **workbench** model, and strict **state / IPC contracts** on the main process.

**Current public build:** **Windows x64** only. **macOS** and **Linux** are planned but **not yet available**.

### Who should read this README

| Goal | Where to start |
|------|----------------|
| **Install and run** the app | [Install](#install) · [Beta program](#beta-program-live) |
| **Product story** (operators / buyers) | [Documentation Canon](docs/CANON.md) · [Wiki overview](docs/wiki/WIKI_PRODUCT_OVERVIEW.md) · [Wiki index](docs/wiki/WIKI_INDEX.md) |
| **Build, test, or cut a release** from source | [Prerequisites](#prerequisites) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Build](#build) · [Release flow](#release-flow) |
| **Agents / automation / repo metrics** | [Agent project status](docs/AGENT_PROJECT_STATUS.md) · [Ultimate playbook](docs/ULTIMATE_PLAYBOOK.md) · `npm run repo:metrics` |

> [!TIP]
> **Source of truth for docs:** [Documentation Canon](docs/CANON.md). For a readable **product** narrative, use the [wiki overview](docs/wiki/WIKI_PRODUCT_OVERVIEW.md) and [wiki index](docs/wiki/WIKI_INDEX.md).

## Install

Download the Windows installer from the [Releases page](https://github.com/Z3r0DayZion-install/NeuralShell/releases) (current line is **v2.1.32** — pick the **latest tag** if it has moved on):

| Platform | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows** x64 | `NeuralShell Setup 2.1.32.exe` | NSIS installer, ~305 MB |

**Verify before running:**

```powershell
# Check the installer hash (match the .exe name to the release you downloaded)
Get-FileHash ".\NeuralShell Setup 2.1.32.exe" -Algorithm SHA256
# Compare against SHA256SUMS.txt, then run the full verification suite:
.\VERIFY_RELEASE.ps1
```

## Beta program (live)

- Recruitment: [Call for Beta Testers](https://github.com/Z3r0DayZion-install/NeuralShell/issues/34)
- Join via forms: [Issue Intake](https://github.com/Z3r0DayZion-install/NeuralShell/issues/new/choose)
- Tester checklist: [BETA_TESTER_CHECKLIST_V2.0-RC-Final.md](docs/pilots/BETA_TESTER_CHECKLIST_V2.0-RC-Final.md)
- Control tower: [Beta Control Tower](https://github.com/Z3r0DayZion-install/NeuralShell/issues/32)

## Launch and marketing assets

- Public launch page source: [docs/index.html](docs/index.html)
- Site asset bundle: [docs/site-assets/asset-manifest.json](docs/site-assets/asset-manifest.json)
- Pricing: [landing/pricing.html](landing/pricing.html)
- Partners: [landing/partners.html](landing/partners.html)
- Press kit: [PRESS_KIT_V2.0-RC-Final.md](docs/pilots/PRESS_KIT_V2.0-RC-Final.md)
- Channel submission: [CHANNEL_SUBMISSION_PLAYBOOK_V2.0-RC-Final.md](docs/pilots/CHANNEL_SUBMISSION_PLAYBOOK_V2.0-RC-Final.md)

## Revenue and growth (maintainers)

Billing, referrals, partners, and related **CLI generators** live in **[docs/README_REVENUE_AND_GROWTH.md](docs/README_REVENUE_AND_GROWTH.md)** so this file stays oriented around **install, trust, and contribution**.

## Enterprise compliance

- SOC2 prep output: `SOC2_PREP_REPORT.md` · collector: `node compliance/soc2_collector.cjs` (map in [CANON](docs/CANON.md))
- Third-party attribution page: `public/about.html` (generate with `node scripts/genAttribution.cjs`)

## Agent marketplace

- Core agent manifests: `agents/core/*/agent.json`
- Install and verify from the in-app **Settings → Agent Marketplace** gallery

## Offline local mode (Ollama)

- Walkthrough: [docs/GETTING_STARTED_OFFLINE_OLLAMA.md](docs/GETTING_STARTED_OFFLINE_OLLAMA.md)
- Operator Home and extensions: [docs/OPERATOR_HOME.md](docs/OPERATOR_HOME.md)
- Canvas quick ops: [docs/CANVAS_QUICK_OPS.md](docs/CANVAS_QUICK_OPS.md)
- When something breaks: [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md)

## For maintainers and contributors

### Quick verification (CI / PR)

```bash
npm run verify:ui:shell
```

See `release/E2E_CORE_UI_PACK.md` and `release/VERIFY_UI_AND_QA_MATRIX.md`. After a **production** desktop build, optional packaged smokes: `npm run verify:smoke:all`.

### Prerequisites

- **Node.js 22.12.x** (see `package.json` **`engines`**).
- Root **`.npmrc`** sets **`engine-strict=true`** — **`npm ci`** fails on the wrong Node version (`EBADENGINE`). [Engines troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#node-npm-engines).

### Quick start

**One-liner (recommended):**

```bash
nvm use 22.12.0 && npm run setup
```

Or step by step:

```bash
nvm use 22.12.0
npm run setup
npm test
npm start
```

### Self-sell proof (demo + evidence)

```powershell
npm run proof:self-sell
```

Artifacts include `screenshots/ui_sales_*.png` and `release/ui-self-sell-proof-report.json`.

### Build

```powershell
npm run icons:generate
npm run build
```

Prepare public site assets and social card:

```powershell
npm run channel:site:prepare
```

### Release flow

Official determinism baseline (Node 22.12.x):

```powershell
npm run proof:bundle
node scripts/release_truth_verify.cjs --determinism-only
```

Standard and strict ship verification:

```powershell
npm run ship
npm run ship:strict
```

**Tag workflow (GitHub Actions):**

1. Ensure `master` has successful **CI**, **Merge Gate**, **Release Contract**, and **Security Gate** runs (or your org’s equivalents).
2. Push a **version tag** that matches **`package.json` `version`** (examples: **`v2.1.32`**, **`v2.2.0-beta.1`**). Avoid stale placeholder tags in internal notes—**the tag drives the release identity**.
3. The **Release** workflow publishes installer, checksums, provenance, and changelog snapshot.

Full operator steps: [RUNBOOK_TAG_RELEASE.md](docs/RUNBOOK_TAG_RELEASE.md)

### Rollback

1. Identify prior stable tag on Releases.
2. Re-point the update channel to previous artifacts (`dist/OMEGA.yml` + installer + blockmap) per runbook.
3. Publish a short rollback note if users must act.

Details: [RUNBOOK_HOTFIX.md](docs/RUNBOOK_HOTFIX.md)

### Troubleshooting (dev and packaged)

- Packaged startup: `npm run diagnose:packaged`
- Strict packaged smoke: `npm run smoke:packaged:strict`
- Release metadata freshness: `npm run release:verify:fresh` and `npm run release:verify:fresh:strict`
- Offline checksum helper:

```powershell
.\scripts\verify.ps1 -SelfTest
.\scripts\verify.ps1
.\scripts\verify.ps1 -Installer
```

- Bypass local pre-push gate once: `$env:NEURAL_SKIP_PREPUSH="1"; git push`
- Validate links under `docs/`, `installer/`, `plugins/`, `beta/`, and root `*.md`: `npm run docs:link-check`
- Milestone checklist: `npm run roadmap:status` · quiet: `npm run roadmap:status -- --quiet` · strict: `npm run roadmap:strict`
- Quick doc pass: `npm run sanity:docs` · full doc contracts: `npm run gate:docs`
- Fragment / anchor checks: GFM slugs; **`DOCS_LINK_CHECK_NO_ANCHORS=1`** disables anchor-only validation if needed.
- Bypass **only** docs link in pre-push: `$env:NEURAL_SKIP_DOCS_LINK_CHECK="1"; git push`
- Bypass **only** roadmap in pre-push: `$env:NEURAL_SKIP_ROADMAP_STATUS="1"; git push`

## Portable mode

- Windows portable guide: [PORTABLE_MODE.md](docs/PORTABLE_MODE.md)

## Security gates

- Dependency review on PRs (`high` severity fails).
- `npm audit --audit-level=high` in CI.
- Secret scan via Gitleaks.
- CodeQL analysis on `master` and PRs.

## Privacy

- [Privacy policy](docs/PRIVACY_POLICY.md)

## Community and wiki

- [Discord server blueprint](docs/community/DISCORD_SERVER_BLUEPRINT.md)
- [Wiki index](docs/wiki/WIKI_INDEX.md)

## License

MIT

Here is what was implemented in `e2e/react-core.spec.js` (no README / workflow edits).

### 1. **Bounded diagnostics** (`offlineKillDiagnosticsSnapshotBestEffort`)
- Wraps `offlineKillDownstreamDiagnostics` in a **wall-clock race** (default callers use **3.2s** before/after, **5.2s** on failure).
- On budget overrun, still writes **`compact`** plus `downstream: { skipped: true, reason: '…', budgetMs }` so failure artifacts land quickly instead of blocking the catch path on another full storage scan + evaluate.

### 2. **`withOfflineKillPrepStage` / `withOfflineKillStage`**
- **Sentinel files:** `offline-kill-prep-${prepName}-entering.json` and `offline-kill-stage-${stageName}-entered.json` with `prep-entering` / `stage-entered` plus budget fields only (no heavy DOM first).
- **before / after / failed** snapshots now use **best-effort diagnostics** instead of unbounded `offlineKillDownstreamDiagnostics`.

### 3. **Storage scan cap** (inside downstream `evaluate`)
- Each of localStorage / sessionStorage is scanned for at most **200** keys so huge stores cannot stall the renderer on every snapshot.

### 4. **Final prep handoff** (`before-provider-stage-entry`)
- Writes **`offline-kill-handoff-provider-stage-entering.json`** first (minimal).
- **`writeCompactOfflineKillSnapshotSafe`** for a compact line in the bundle.
- **`offline-kill-prep-before-provider-stage-entry-snapshot.json`** uses **bounded** diagnostics (**2.2s**), not a full unbounded downstream pull.
- **`PREP_BEFORE_PROVIDER_MS`** raised **10s → 14s** so this handoff stays inside the prep wall with the extra small files.

### 5. **`openrouter-lane` wall clock**
- **`PREP_OPENROUTER_MS`** **20s → 36s** so slow CI can finish preset / option detection once diagnostics no longer steal time from the inner `Promise.race`.

## `selectProviderValue` (OpenRouter offline-kill path)

- **Inner budget**: `providerSelectBudgetMs = min(36000, max(4000, stageRemainingMsFn() - 2500))`, with `remainingProviderSelectMs()` enforced via `budgetAssert` before scroll / visible / enabled / select / poll / fallback.
- **Per-step caps** (each timeout capped by remaining budget): scroll **3s**, visible **5s**, enabled **5s**, `selectOption` **6s** (also capped by `selectTimeoutMs`), poll **8s**; fixed `waitForTimeout` sleeps are clipped by remaining budget.
- **Artifacts** (only when `value === 'openrouter'`):  
  `offline-kill-provider-select-openrouter-{entered,before-select,after-select-attempt,after-dom-fallback,after-success,failed,failed-diagnostics}.json` (fallback / success / diagnostics only when those paths run).
- **Classifications** (including your list): e.g. `provider-select-option-missing`, `provider-select-control-missing`, `provider-select-control-hidden`, `provider-select-control-disabled`, `provider-select-playwright-timeout`, `provider-select-value-stuck-ollama`, `provider-select-event-not-fired`, `provider-select-dom-fallback-worked` / `provider-select-dom-fallback-failed`, `provider-select-app-state-reverted`, `provider-select-helper-timeout`, `provider-select-page-closed`, `provider-select-retry-failed` (second attempt maps most failures here with `innerClassification`), `provider-select-retry-skipped-budget-exhausted`.
- **Minimal first**: `failed.json` uses `providerSelectMinimalContext` (no storage walk); `failed-diagnostics.json` adds `offlineKillDiagnosticsSnapshotBestEffort(..., 1800)` plus `providerStateSnapshotBounded(..., 1200)`.
- **Legacy compact files** kept where useful (`offline-kill-compact-provider-openrouter-*-failed.json` on some branches); full `providerStateSnapshot` before select is **not** used on the OpenRouter path (replaced by `before-select` + minimal context). Non–OpenRouter calls still use the old `offline-kill-compact-${label}-before-commit-probe.json` path.

- **`ensureConnectionPanel`**: `visibilityTimeout = min(STAGE_PHASE_MS, max(5000, remain - 8500))`.
- **`withOfflineKillStage(..., 'provider-select-openrouter', ...)`**: `resolveClassification` prefers `err.providerSelectClassification` so the stage `*-failed.json` shows the **inner** class when the helper threw first.

## Commit `cd9a67d` — `test: fail fast when offline kill settings click does not open drawer`

### What changed (`openSettingsDrawerForOfflineKill`)

1. **After `first-click-no-drawer.json`**  
   - If the page is closed → existing `settings-open-page-closed-before-recovery` + throw.  
   - If `remainingOpenSettingsMs() < 12000` → **`writeFailed('settings-drawer-open-timeout-after-first-click', …, { phase: 'first-click-no-drawer' })`** and throw (no recovery).

2. **Recovery** (`runOpenSettingsRecovery`)  
   - Still requires **`MIN_RECOVERY_HELPER_MS` (12s)** before starting.  
   - **`assertRemaining`** before dismiss / retry click / drawer wait so the **32s helper** fails with **`settings-open-recovery-skipped-budget-exhausted`** instead of stalling.  
   - Per-step caps: dismiss **2500ms**, opener visible **2500ms**, retry click **4000ms**, drawer **6000ms** (via `stepTimeout`).

3. **No global `Promise.race` on the whole recovery**  
   A single wall (9–16s) was killing valid recoveries locally (drawer sometimes >16s). Recovery is bounded by those **per-step** timeouts + **`assertRemaining`**, not an extra wall clock race.

4. **`settings-open-recovery-timeout`**  
   On **timeout-like** recovery errors (and not page-closed), write **`offline-kill-open-settings-${label}-recovery-timeout.json`**, then **`writeFailed('settings-open-recovery-timeout', …)`**.

5. **`writeFailed`**  
   - Adds cheap **`drawerCount` / `openDrawerCount`**.  
   - **`failed-diagnostics`**: `offlineKillOpenSettingsDiagnosticsBestEffort(pg, 1500)` raced with **1650ms** ceiling so diagnostics cannot block the throw.

### Scope

- **`e2e/react-core.spec.js`** only for behavior.  
- **`governance/source_manifest.json`** via `npm run governance:sync`.

Both Playwright greps, `lint`, `docs:link-check`, `npm test`, `governance:sync`, `test:integrity`: **green**.

You asked for a **~9s total `Promise.race`** around recovery; that made the offline-kill test fail whenever recovery needed a bit longer. From the failed job log attachment list:

1. **`offline-kill-open-settings-offline-kill-failed.json`** — **present** (listed twice with the same hash; reporter duplication). This is the right bucket for an inner open-settings failure.
2. **`offline-kill-open-settings-offline-kill-recovery-timeout.json`** — **not** listed.

4. **`offline-kill-provider-select-openrouter-*.json`** — **not** listed; flow did **not** hand off to provider-select.
5. Later **`offline-kill-stage-*`** — not the deciding layer here.
6. **Green Verify UI** — no.

**Sequence implied by snapshots:** `entered` → `before-click` → `after-click` → **`first-click-no-drawer`** → then the early stage lost the race.

**Playwright’s reported error** is still:

`[offline-kill-early] open-settings exceeded 45000ms`

So you **did** get the bad outcome again: the **outer 45s early wrapper** is what the test throws, even though inner open-settings artifacts (including **`first-click-no-drawer`**) were written.

The minimal CI artifact for this run is only a marker file, so the **exact `classification` string inside `offline-kill-open-settings-offline-kill-failed.json`** is not available locally without the full **`test-results`** zip from the job.

## Likely mechanism (why outer 45s can still win)

`withOfflineKillEarlyStage` uses **`Promise.race([fn(), timeoutPromise])`**. The inner helper’s own deadline is **32s** from **`openSettingsDrawerForOfflineKill`’s `started`**, while the early timer is **45s** from when the timer is armed (right after early `before` snapshots). There is a **~13s** window where **`fn()` can still be awaiting a Playwright call** after the helper budget is gone.

In `stepTimeout`, when **`remaining <= safetyFloorMs`**, the code returns **`0`**. Those zeros are passed into **`expect(..., { timeout: ... })`** and **`click({ timeout: ... })`**. In this repo, **`playwright.e2e.config.js`** sets **`expect.timeout: 25000`** and **`actionTimeout: 30000`**, so a **`0`** timeout is very plausibly reinterpreted as a **long default**, which can keep **`fn()`** pending until the **45s** early timer wins—exactly the failure shape you see, possibly **without** going through the recovery-timeout attachment path.

## What would prove the patch (this run)

- **Partial:** Inner **`offline-kill-open-settings-offline-kill-failed.json`** + **`first-click-no-drawer`** show the harness is naming the stuck phase more than a bare stage timeout.
- **Not achieved:** The thrown error is still the **outer 45s** line, and there is **no** provider-select artifact.

## Suggested next code move (small, targeted)

Clamp or forbid **`0`** Playwright timeouts on this path (e.g. never pass **`timeout: 0`** to `expect` / `click`; or treat **`stepTimeout(...) <= 0`** as an immediate **`assertRemaining` / `writeFailed`** path). That keeps **`fn()`** from outliving the early race on “default” assertion timeouts.
